title: Fabrication constraints connected to the design interface: measured minimum linewidth and gap by morphological opening, perturbation evaluated with the forward, binary export

fixture.gap_violation: tests/test_design_workflow.py: 12 x 12 logits of +-8 forming two solid blocks (columns 1..4 and 6..10 of rows 1..10) separated by one 0.1 um pixel, DensityParameterization with filter_radius_um 0.15, truncate boundary, beta 64, eta 0.5; DesignProblem with a linear objective (density times a linspace weight); fabrication(spacing 0.1 um, min_linewidth 0.15 um, min_gap 0.15 um, perturbation 0.1 um)
fixture.feature_measurement: tests/test_design_workflow.py: 30 x 1 periodic line with runs of 4, 1 and 8 pixels (0.05 um); 12 x 12 blocks of 5 x 5 and 4 x 5 pixels one pixel apart at the array edge (0.1 um), measured with extend and periodic boundaries; a uniform 5 x 5 design
fixture.binary_export: tests/test_design_workflow.py: 6 x 5 binary with three rectangular runs, origin (-0.6, -0.5) um, 0.2 um pixels, z from -0.1 to 0.1 um
fixture.examples: the fabrication reports of examples/design_metagrating.py (spacing 0.05 um, declared min linewidth and gap 0.1 um, perturbation 0.05 um, periodic x) and examples/design_mode_coupler.py (spacing 0.2 um, declared 0.4 um, perturbation 0.2 um) as run by the G6-05 end-to-end tests and the G6-07 recorded starts
fixture.measurement: torchfdtd.fabrication: opening by digital squares of every integer side (odd sides centred on a pixel, even sides on a corner); the minimum linewidth is the largest side whose opening leaves the solid unchanged, the minimum gap the same on the void; erosion and dilation by the square of side 2 amount + 1

reference_method: Analytic discrete morphology: a run of L pixels or a rectangle of W by H pixels survives the opening with side s exactly when min(W, H) >= s, so the measured values are known by construction (linewidth 4, gap 1 for the gap-violation blocks; 4 and 6 for the periodic line; 5 and 1 with extend, 4 with periodic for the edge blocks). The perturbation changes are the forward model's own responses to the eroded and dilated designs; they are recorded and required to be finite and nonzero, not compared to an external value.

observables.name: measured_gap_pixels
observables.definition: gap_pixels of the thresholded gap-violation design

observables.name: measured_linewidth_pixels
observables.definition: linewidth_pixels of the thresholded gap-violation design

observables.name: violations
observables.definition: FeatureSizes.violations against the declared 0.15 um limits

observables.name: structure_tiling
observables.definition: the exported rectangles cover exactly the solid pixels without overlap

acceptance.perturbation_objective_change: finite and nonzero for both erosion and dilation; eroded solid fraction below dilated
acceptance.source_of_limits: analytic discrete morphology on declared arrays; the filter radius alone is explicitly not accepted as a minimum-feature guarantee

tests/test_design_workflow.py::test_meas.oracle: gap and linewidth known by construction; perturbation change recorded from the objective

tests/test_design_workflow.py::test_feat.oracle: run lengths and rectangle sides known by construction, both boundary rules

tests/test_design_workflow.py::test_bina.oracle: pixel coverage recomputed from the rectangles

not_yet_covered: a fabrication-constrained optimization (penalty or projection that enforces the measured minimum feature during the optimization); the measurement reports, it does not constrain
sub-pixel perturbation amounts (the erosion and dilation move whole pixels)
curved or diagonal features, for which the square element is a Manhattan measure

error_budget.precision_floor: none for the morphology (integer pixels); float32 for the objective changes

notes: torchfdtd/fabrication.py is added with this case. The first draft measured with digital disks and reported a 5 x 5 square as 3 pixels wide because a disk cannot fill a right-angle corner; the element was changed to digital squares before the recorded run and the definition is stated in the module and in docs/DESIGN_WORKFLOW.md. Exported rectangles are widened by 1e-9 um so that a Yee node on a pixel edge is material whichever side it rounds to (the same rule the polygon importer applies); the first coupler pilot without this widening showed a 0.026 GDS difference that was floating-point rounding, not geometry.
